- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or high historical values.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when true outcomes show strong mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after a spike in history, then gradually corrects — model should apply a dampening factor to avoid overcorrection.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon; should increase sensitivity to recent low values.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values when history includes high volatility or recent high peaks — apply downward adjustment based on recent 7-day average.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging true price drops; consider using a 10–15 day moving average to reduce lag.
- When true outcome shows a strong downward trend after a peak, model should reduce forecast slope more aggressively than linear interpolation.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; should smooth out forecast with exponential decay or weighted average of recent 5–7 days.
